metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: fragility fracture.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: may cause glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis. The committee agreed that people

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: should have a risk assessment. FRAX includes glucocorticoid exposure as a risk

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: factor, defined as current or prior use of oral glucocorticoids at a dose equivalent to

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: doses. The committee also agreed that people who take higher doses intermittently,

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: for example using 3 or more rescue packs of glucocorticoids for respiratory or other

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: inflammatory conditions, are also at risk of fragility fracture. They also noted that

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: insufficiency. This condition causes low levels of endogenous corticosteroids, so a

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: replacement dose is needed. As long as the physiological equivalent dose is not

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: exceeded then this does not increase the person's risk of fragility fracture.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: Why the committee made the recommendations

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: When assessing risk in people aged 30 and over, the committee agreed that either

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: FRAX or QFracture should be used. This is similar to the recommendation made in the

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: 2012 NICE guideline on osteoporosis because recent evidence has not shown an

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: advantage of using 1 tool over the other. For people who have not had a previous hip

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: or vertebral fragility fracture, a single major osteoporotic fragility fracture in the last

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: 2 years, or 2 or more fragility fractures, the committee agreed that it is best to use a

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: risk prediction tool first because it helps avoid unnecessary DXA scans. FRAX only

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: applies to people over the age of 40, so the committee recommended using QFracture for people between the ages of 30 and 39. A 10-year risk of major osteoporotic fracture is generally used when calculating risk from FRAX or QFracture, so the

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: committee recommended this.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: Risk prediction tools may not provide an accurate assessment of risk in people

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: over 90. So, the committee agreed healthcare professionals would need to take this

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: into account when using risk tools for this age group. In this group, FRAX calculates

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: risk by assuming the person is aged 90. While QFracture can provide a risk score for

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: people up to the age of 99, it covers fewer years. For example, it will estimate an 8-year risk score for people aged 92 or a 7-year risk score for people aged 93. But the committee agreed that this would still provide useful information when assessing a

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: person's risk.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: The committee emphasised the importance of doing a full clinical risk assessment

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: because neither tool includes all factors associated with an increased risk of fracture

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: (for example, if a person is taking medicines associated with accelerated bone loss

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: such as aromatase inhibitors or androgen deprivation therapy). They also noted that

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: the same risk prediction tool should be used throughout a person's care. This is

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: because FRAX and QFracture assess risk differently, for example, quantity-dependent

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: risk factors may not be treated as continuous variables. Alcohol intake is measured in

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: FRAX as either over or under 3 units per day, whereas in QFracture there are several

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: levels of alcohol intake. FRAX also has fewer criteria than QFracture so is less

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: detailed. In contrast, FRAX gives a risk score adjusted for mortality whereas QFracture

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: does not. QFracture also includes oestrogen-only hormone replacement therapy

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: (HRT) use in its assessment. The committee agreed that when doing the risk

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: assessment, it is important to take into account that systemic HRT can reduce the risk

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: of fracture.

metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: When assessing fragility fractures for some groups the committee agreed that advice

text: Why the committee made the recommendations

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: The committee discussed that vertebral fractures are the most common type of

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: osteoporotic fracture but people often have no symptoms and so they can go

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: undiagnosed. Identifying a vertebral fracture is important because it may mean

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: someone's condition is eligible for treatment that would not be otherwise or that a

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: different treatment is needed. Vertebral fracture assessment (VFA) adds some

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: additional time to a DXA scan and for reviewing and reporting but will lead to

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: reductions in fractures through improved treatment. It could reduce reliance on

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: conventional radiography to identify vertebral fractures and exposure to higher doses

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: of ionising radiation. People would also benefit from having all relevant scans on the

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: same visit rather than having a DXA scan and then needing to return for further

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: radiography in a separate visit.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: Cost-effectiveness evidence was available in people 50 years and over with a fracture

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: having a DXA scan and people aged 65 to 80 years at high risk of vertebral fracture

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: having a DXA scan. But the committee agreed that because of current low

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: identification rates of vertebral fractures, wider recommendations to consider VFA

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: when doing DXA scans were likely to be cost effective. They prioritised

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: recommendations for groups where risk of vertebral fracture was higher.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: The committee was aware of evidence suggesting a higher incidence of vertebral

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: fractures in men aged 70 and over and women aged 60 and over. So, they agreed that

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: people in this age range who are having a DXA scan should also be considered for a

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: VFA at the same visit.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: This evidence also suggested men aged under 70 and women aged under 60 are less

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: likely to have a vertebral fracture. So, the committee agreed that DXA-based VFA

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: should only be for people at high risk of having a vertebral fracture in this age group.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: The committee agreed that DXA-based VFA should not be done if the person has had

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: recent spinal imaging and no symptoms because it is unlikely to identify a fracture.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: They also agreed that it should not be done if the person has scoliosis that is likely to

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: affect the interpretation (for example, severe scoliosis can make it difficult to interpret

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: the results) or their body mass exceeds local guidelines because the scan results

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: would not be easy to interpret accurately.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: Several studies suggested that doing a VFA when doing a DXA scan had a low risk of

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: misdiagnosing vertebral fractures with high specificity reported in the per-vertebral

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: analysis from low-quality evidence. This means that if DXA-based VFA positively

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: identifies a person as having a fracture, it is highly likely to be accurate. So, the

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: committee recommended that if a person's VFA is positive, then there is no need to do

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: further spinal imaging unless there are specific concerns. These could include an

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: uncertainty from a borderline VFA scan, or the fracture could be caused by a different

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: condition to osteoporosis, such as a pathological fracture in a person with a history of

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: breast cancer.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: Most evidence on accuracy of DXA-based VFA scans uses older scanners and shows

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: low specificity. Recent scanners have increased image quality and resolution, which

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: should result in better accuracy (for both sensitivity and specificity) for detecting

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: vertebral fractures. So, the committee made a recommendation for research on the

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: accuracy of DXA-based VFA.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: How the recommendations might affect practice

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: able to be accommodated within existing DXA slots but appropriate scheduling of

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: Ensuring sufficient reporting capacity is available will be important for

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: implementation. There may also be additional staff training costs to enable expanded

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: access. Increased capital investment is not anticipated because most current DXA

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: scanners have the capacity to do VFA.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: In some areas, it is common to do spinal imaging to confirm a vertebral fracture

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: identified on VFA. Where VFA is currently used, it will displace spinal imaging to look

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: for vertebral fracture at lower cost in some people. But the population recommended

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: for VFA will be broader than that currently having spinal radiograph and a small

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: proportion of VFA results may need a subsequent spinal image when there is

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: uncertainty. Overall, a net reduction in spinal images is anticipated.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: Increased use of VFA in the NHS is expected to increase identification of vertebral

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: fractures, which are often missed in current practice. This is expected to result in

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: increased and better targeted treatment that will reduce fractures.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: The committee concluded that the overall financial impact of the new

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: recommendations on the NHS is not likely to be significant over the long term.

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: Fractures associated with osteoporosis, typically caused by low-impact injuries that would

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: not normally cause a fracture (such as a fall from standing height) and sometimes called

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: low-trauma fractures. Fragility fractures can occur spontaneously in people with no history

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: of injury. Most vertebral fragility fractures are not caused by falls, instead happening after

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: activities involving lifting, twisting, or bending. Fragility fractures most commonly affect

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)
metadata.title: Osteoporosis: assessing the risk of fragility fracture (NG259)

text: the spine (vertebral column), hip, shoulder (proximal humerus), and wrist (distal forearm).

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

metadata.source_org: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)

text: EVIDENCE ASSESSMENT The USPSTF concludes with moderate certainty that screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in women 65 years or older has moderate net benefit. The USPSTF concludes with moderate certainty that screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in postmenopausal women younger than 65 years at increased risk has moderate net benefit. The USPSTF concludes that the evidence is insufficient and the balance of benefits and harms for screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in men cannot be determined.

text: RECOMMENDATION The USPSTF recommends screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in women 65 years or older. (B recommendation) The USPSTF recommends screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in postmenopausal women younger than 65 years who are at increased risk for an osteoporotic fracture as estimated by clinical risk assessment. (B recommendation) The USPSTF concludes that the current evidence is insufficient to assess the balance of benefits and harms of screening for osteoporosis to prevent osteoporotic fractures in men. metadata.source_org: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF)
metadata.title: Screening for Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures

text: These recommendations apply to adults 40 years or older without known osteoporosis or history of fragility fractures. They do not apply to persons with secondary osteoporosis due to an underlying medical condition (eg, cancer, metabolic bone diseases, or hyperthyroidism) or chronic use of a medication (eg, glucocorticoids) associated with bone loss.

text: How to implement this recommendation?

metadata.source_org: U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF)
metadata.title: Screening for Osteoporosis to Prevent Fractures

text: Screen women 65 years or older with DXA BMD, with or without fracture risk assessment. • For postmenopausal women younger than 65 years, the USPSTF suggests first assessing for the presence of 1 or more risk factors for osteoporosis. For women who have 1 or more risk factors, assess for increased risk using a clinical risk assessment tool. For women assessed to be at increased risk, screen for osteoporosis with DXA BMD, with or without fracture risk assessment.

text: To achieve the benefit of screening to reduce morbidity and mortality from fractures, women found to have osteoporosis should be further evaluated, counseled, and, if appropriate, receive evidence-based care management.

text: Osteoporotic fractures are associated with psychological distress, subsequent fractures, loss of independence, reduced ability to perform activities of daily living, and death. Evidence shows that only 40% to 60% of persons experiencing a hip fracture recover their prefracture level of mobility and ability to perform activities of daily living.
